title: How Microsegmentation resource policies, perimeter policies and policy settings work

prose.text: {{policy-layers}} What a policy can be applied between is stated differently by the resource group article {{divergence:policy-endpoints}}.

prose.label: Open questions.
prose.text: What Sim Block does is not defined {{gap:sim-block-meaning}}, and the UDP Include-all wording is unclear {{gap:udp-include-all-wording}}.

prose.label: Related.
prose.text: Recommendations that create policies are in [[zms.policy-recommendations]] and the groups they connect in [[zms.resources]].

checks.do: Whether a rule with a lower priority integer already matches the traffic.
Whether the Default Resource Policy Rule setting is Allow for traffic no other policy covers.

settings-global.statement: The Policy Settings page controls policy enforcement globally; its Default Resource Policy Rule (Allow) is the catch-all for the whole organization's traffic when other policies do not apply, and settings must be confirmed before taking effect.

quotes: admins can control policy enforcement settings at a global level.
Click Allow for Default Resource Policy Rule.
This rule is what the system defaults to if other policies don’t apply to the traffic observed.
The scope of this policy acts as a catch-all for the entirety of your organization
You are prompted to confirm policy settings before they take effect.

policy-layers.statement: The Configuring Microsegmentation Policies article says enforcement policies are Layer 3 and Layer 4, protect east-west traffic in cloud and data center environments, and are applied between resource groups or between a resource group and any other resource.

quotes: Admins can create Layer 3 and Layer 4 Microsegmentation enforcement policies to protect east-west traffic in both cloud and data center environments.
Policies are applied between resource groups or between a resource group and any other resource.

priority-order.statement: Policies are evaluated from highest priority (lowest integer) to lowest priority (highest integer), no two policies can share a priority, and the maximum rule order depends on how many rules exist.

quotes: Policies are evaluated from highest priority (lowest integer) to lowest priority (highest integer). No two policies can have the same priority.
The maximum number possible depends on how many existing rules there are in the list.

rule-actions.statement: A policy rule Action is Allow, Sim Block or Block.

quotes: Action: Select Allow, Sim Block, or Block.

rule-limits.statement: A rule takes up to 10 sources, up to 10 destinations, and up to 10 TCP and 10 UDP additional port ranges, or an Include-all toggle for TCP or UDP ports.

quotes: You can select up to 10 sources total.
You can select up to 10 destinations total.
Click Add TCP Port Range to add up to 10 ranges, or enable the toggle Include all TCP ports
Click Add UDP Port Range to add up to 10 ranges, or enable the toggle Include all UDP ports

rule-scope.statement: A rule's Scope is the AppZones it affects; Include all AppZones is selected by default.

quotes: Scope: Select or deselect the checkbox to Include all AppZones. By default, it is already selected.
Scope: The AppZone the policy rule should affect.

rule-app-ports.statement: A rule's destination can use an application port template drawn from the Application Catalog, which then shows the ports associated with the application.

quotes: Destination application port template: Select from the drop-down menu applications that are in the Application Catalog. When you select an application, it appears in a table that displays the ports associated with it.

list-columns.statement: The Resource Policies page lists each rule's Order (which is applied first), Source, Destination, Applications, Protocol, Scope, Rule Action and Last Hit.

quotes: Order: The ranking of which policy rule should be applied first.
Scope: The AppZone the policy rule should affect.
Source: The source location for the policy rule.
Destination: The destination location for the policy rule.
Protocol: The protocols added to the policy rule.
Rule Action: The command for the policy rule to apply.
Applications: The applications associated with the policy rule, if any.
Last Hit: The last time the policy rule was triggered.

changes-immediate.statement: Configurations, edits and deletions of policy rules take effect immediately.

quotes: Any configurations, edits, or deletions of policy rules take effect immediately.

perimeter-purpose.statement: Perimeter policies define how Microsegmentation handles inbound, outbound and internal traffic for managed resource groups.

quotes: Perimeter policies allow you to easily define how Microsegmentation handles inbound, outbound, and internal traffic for managed resource groups.

perimeter-fields.statement: A perimeter policy sets Inbound and Outbound Traffic Enforcement to Sim Block, Block or Disable and Internal Traffic Enforcement to Allow or Disable; it is ordered last by default.

quotes: Inbound Traffic Enforcement: Select Sim Block, Block, or Disable.
Outbound Traffic Enforcement: Select Sim Block, Block, or Disable.
Internal Traffic Enforcement: Select Allow or Disable.
The policy is ordered last by default.

perimeter-delete-confirm.statement: Deleting a perimeter policy at Zero Trust Cloud > Microsegmentation > Perimeter Policies requires entering CONFIRM in the Delete Perimeter Policy Rule window.

quotes: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Cloud > Microsegmentation > Perimeter Policies.
The Delete Perimeter Policy Rule window appears.
Enter CONFIRM.

perimeter-edit-rg.statement: When editing a perimeter policy the Resource Group field cannot be changed.

quotes: You cannot edit the Resource Group field.

policy-endpoints.summary: The resource group article says policies apply to traffic between two resource groups; the policy configuration article says they apply between resource groups or between a resource group and any other resource.

positions.says: Policies are applied to traffic between two resource groups.

quotes: Policies are applied to traffic between two resource groups.

positions.says: Policies are applied between resource groups or between a resource group and any other resource.

quotes: Policies are applied between resource groups or between a resource group and any other resource.

policy-endpoints.impact: Whether a rule's source or destination can be something other than a resource group depends on which article is followed; the captures do not reconcile them.

sim-block-meaning.title: What Sim Block does as a policy action
sim-block-meaning.detail: The articles list Sim Block beside Allow and Block as a rule action, a perimeter enforcement choice and a flow log action, and none defines it.

udp-include-all-wording.title: What the Include all UDP ports toggle covers
udp-include-all-wording.detail: The configuring article words it "Include all UDP ports to add all available TCP port ranges"; this is probably a typo, and the captured text does not resolve it.
